partners.diseaseBName: hereditary arterial and articular multiple calcification syndrome
partners.mechanism_chain:
NT5E (HGNC:8005) —DECREASES→ AMP (CHEBI:16135); NT5E (HGNC:8005) —DISRUPTS→ ATP (CHEBI:15422); AMP (CHEBI:16135) —LEADS_TO→ Adenosine production (GO:0006163); NT5C2 (HGNC:8004) —DECREASES→ Inorganic pyrophosphate (PPi) (CHEBI:17677); NT5C2 (HGNC:8004) —DISRUPTS→ Mineralization (GO:0001503); Adenosine production (GO:0006163) —LEADS_TO→ Mineralization (GO:0001503); Mineralization (GO:0001503) —LEADS_TO→ Arterial calcification (HP:0002654); Mineralization (GO:0001503) —LEADS_TO→ Articular calcification (HP:0002779). Loss-of-function mutations in NT5E (encoding Ectonucleotidase 5
' E5) impair its ability to hydrolyze extracellular ATP to AMP and adenosine, potentially leading to altered purinergic signaling and impaired vascular smooth muscle cell differentiation involved in vascular calcification. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in NT5C2, which encodes a 5'-nucleotidase that hydrolyzes AMP to adenosine and inorganic phosphate, disrupt the normal balance of nucleotide metabolites. This disruption, particularly the reduced production of inorganic pyrophosphate (a known inhibitor of calcification), contributes to abnormal mineralization. Both pathways converge on the dysregulation of mineralization processes, leading to arterial and articular calcification.
